text:
maria: Quick flag — billing noticed a ~38% jump in trace storage last month. We don't have a single canonical retention policy across environments and it's making cost forecasting hard. Can we land on defaults and an enforcement plan?

ajay: +1. We also have users complaining about slow long-range trace queries when data moves to cold. Need to balance searchability vs cost.

kim: Can we start with concrete buckets? My proposal: prod = 30d 'hot' searchable, 180d "warm" (index-light, limited query), >180d archived (s3 glacier-like, non-searchable). staging/dev = 7d hot, 30d archived. Default workspace-level overrides allowed for paid customers.

derek: I worry about the semantics of "warm". If we remove indices for warm, dashboards that currently query 90d will break. We should define which query types are allowed against warm. Maybe keep trace metadata index for 180d but evict full span blobs.

elaine: +1 to Derek. Many SREs use trace timelines across 3 months for regressions. If we keep only partial index we need an explicit UX (Console: ‘search scope: hot/warm/archived’) and a UX prompt when query will be slow.

maria: Good points. Two parallel threads: storage policy itself, and console/alerting/UX for when traces live in warm/archived. For policy enforcement: lifecycle vs DB TTL vs explicit archiver?

ajay: We should prefer immutable object storage lifecycle where possible. Example S3 rule for moving objects after N days:
```json
{
  "Rules": [
    {
      "ID": "move-to-warm",
      "Prefix": "traces/prod/",
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "Transitions": [
        {"Days": 30, "StorageClass": "STANDARD_IA"},
        {"Days": 180, "StorageClass": "GLACIER"}
      ],
      "Expiration": {"Days": 365}
    }
  ]
}
```
Downside: lifecycle moves objects but our search indices (Dynamo/ES) still contain pointers and cost to keep them up to date.

kim: What about TTL at the span index level? We could keep an ES/Dynamo TTL policy that drops span docs after 30 days for prod, 7 days for dev. But then you lose the ability to reconstruct traces even if the blobs exist. We could keep a compact trace index with key metadata for 180 days and drop detailed span docs sooner.

derek: This is where sampling matters. For high-QPS services we should keep full spans for 30d, then sample 1% for long-term. Maybe a combination: per-service hot window + global cold sampling. Tail-sampling for errors should be retained longer regardless of env.

elaine: Requirements we need captured: 1) SLO/regression investigations need 90d of error traces for prod; 2) security/forensics may request 1yr for some regulated customers (enterprise only); 3) non-prod teams prefer cheap defaults.

maria: Proposed defaults (starting point):
- prod: hot_full_spans = 30d; warm_meta_index = 180d; cold_archive_blob = 365d (configurable per org)
- preprod/staging: hot = 14d; warm_meta = 60d; cold = 180d
- dev/feature: hot = 3d; archive = 30d
- enterprise / compliance override: single-tenant retention up to 1yr with support ticket

ajay: Mechanisms to implement:
- exporter tagging (OTEL) adds env and org labels so lifecycle rules can mark objects by prefix (traces/{org}/{env}/...)
- indexing pipeline creates two indices: span_detail (hot TTL) and trace_catalog (metadata long TTL)
- archiver job that verifies integrity before moving blobs and updates catalog pointers

kim: We need a migration path for existing data. A one-shot backfill archiver that re-writes objects with the new prefix structure so lifecycle rules pick them up. That job needs to be rate-limited. ops-bot, can we schedule a low-IO window?

ops-bot: Scheduled: low-io window queued for Sun 02:00-06:00 UTC next weekend. Archiver backfill job will spawn with concurrency=8 and rate-limit=200 MB/s. See https://internal/redwood/ops/jobs#archiver for details. :gear:

derek: Implementation risk: search latency spike when we compact indices or reindex. Need canary and telemetry docs on query error rates. Also must add a migration flag to roll back if dashboards break.

elaine: UX asks: Console should surface retention per workspace and per-route (some services export more spans). Add query hint: "Data in warm storage — broad queries may take minutes". Also add an action: "Request restore" for critical trace retrieval that kicks off a temporary restore from cold to warm for up to X hours.

maria: For enforcement: prefer immutable storage lifecycle + index TTL + archiver metadata tombstones. Reason: lifecycle is reliable and offloads work to S3; index TTL ensures we don't continue to pay indexing cost. Archiver maintains pointer health so Console shows where trace lives.

ajay: Cost model: estimate per-org hot-window cost = (ingest_rate_tokens * avg_span_size * hot_days) * cost_per_gb + index_multiplier. We should add a per-org alert for projected overage when hot window exceeds baseline by 20%.

kim: Also consider retention-specific quotas: e.g., default hot retention for free tier limited to 14d; paid can increase. That reduces surprise bills.

derek: For exporters: require OTEL batch processor to include the header `x-rw-org` or set resource attribute `service.namespace` so we can partition early. Example config snippet: 
```yaml
exporters:
  rw_s3:
    type: s3
    bucket: redwood-traces
    prefix: "${resource.service.namespace}/${env}/"
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 5s
    send_batch_size: 512
```

elaine: A couple of edge cases: 1) Traces with PII that must be purged ASAP — we need a 'jurisdictional purge' API that invalidates archived blobs and removes catalog entries; 2) When customer requests data export, we must ensure exported artifacts honor retention rules (i.e., cannot re-ingest to bypass TTL).

maria: Next steps:
- Draft formal policy doc and default numbers (I'll sketch today)
- Eng-platform: design lifecycle + index TTL + archiver workflow (owner: Ajay)
- Console: retention UX mocks + 'restore/request' flow (owner: Elaine)
- Eng-ML: sampling heuristics for long-term retention (owner: Kim)
- Ops: schedule backfill and run canary (owner: Derek + ops-bot)

ajay: I'll put up a PR with the lifecycle rules + example index templates and a small cost calc sheet.

kim: I'll prototype a downsampling pipeline that keeps error traces fully and samples normal traces. Will include a tail-sampling snippet.

derek: I'll add telemetry alerts for query error rate/regression and a rollback playbook.

maria: Thanks all. Let's aim to finalize defaults by EOD Thursday so legal/compliance can review. :thumbsup:
